A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CALD research. Their complete main text, Appendices A-C, equations, tables, figures, and algorithms are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original model-conversion experiments in Tables 1-3, hidden-state analyses in Figures 3-4, and computational measurements in Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results, including language and speech benchmarks, hidden-state analyses, and timing measurements.

M1.justification: CALD's parameter transfer, distillation losses, target/trajectory/waypoint guidance, hybrid procedure, and architecture conversions are unchanged. Appendix B retains the same three training algorithms.

E1.justification: Both versions use QNLI, QQP, SST2, IMDB, the same Pile subsets and downstream language-model evaluations, and TED-LIUMv3, SLURP, and VoxCeleb1. Appendix C retains the same audio-length timing scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain identical comparator membership: the corresponding standard transformers, unguided conversion, experiment-specific CALD variants, and the published pretrained-Linformer comparison in Table 1.

E3.justification: The model sizes, training budgets, Pile fractions, metrics, checkpoint schedules, and analysis sample sizes remain unchanged in Section 4. Appendix A retains the same experimental settings and hyperparameters.

E4.justification: Both retain the source-initialization comparison, hidden-state cosine-distance and t-SNE analyses, and observation that speech training without parameter transfer fails to converge well. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Figure 5 reports averaging five timing runs in both versions. Benchmark seed information, uncertainty reporting, and statistical testing practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Results in Tables 1-3, Figures 3-5, and Appendix C are unchanged. For example, trajectory-guided Linformer averages 92.5% accuracy and hybrid speech conversion achieves 6.41% ASR WER in both versions.

T1.justification: Equations (1)-(7) and their mathematical definitions retain the same content. No formal assumptions, derivations, theorems, or proofs are introduced or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about joint fine-tuning and conversion, applicability across speech and language models, and recovering performance close to the original transformers.

C2.justification: The explanations connecting guidance effectiveness to hidden-state shifts remain unchanged. The resource limitation restricting language-model experiments to Pythia-1B and the qualification that inference speed depends on implementation are also retained.

D1.justification: Section 1 replaces the promise that code and models will become public with a statement of availability and a specific reproduction-repository link. This adds concrete access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, algorithms, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged. Mamba, Linearizing Large Language Models, SSAMBA, and The Mamba in the Llama receive publication-metadata updates identifying the same previously cited works.

P1.justification: v3 updates the running header to ICLR 2025 publication status, adds a funding acknowledgement, revises the resource-availability sentence, and updates bibliographic metadata. The scientific narrative and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: The repository statement and acknowledgements produce limited text reflow, spacing adjustments, and reference-pagination shifts. All five figures, four tables, and three algorithm displays retain their designs and placement.

improvement.justification: Replacing a future-release promise with a specific reproduction-repository link modestly improves reproducibility documentation. The scientific methods, evidence, and limitations are unchanged, while the remaining edits concern publication information and presentation.
